title: Fix Sunshine service name in omarchy-install-service-sunshine
head: 084538cfe124
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The now-working installer starts a published vulnerable Sunshine build on the stable and rc channels
leads.consequence: On stock stable/rc, omarchy-pkg-add sunshine selects 2026.516.143833-4.1 and the new line starts it, then firewall rules open streaming ports to private networks. Upstream's 2026.906.222525 release fixes five published issues affecting this version (including a pairing approval mix-up and, during active streaming, an unauthenticated control-stream denial of service); 2026.914.233613 additionally fixes a high-severity Linux capability issue affecting this build. A user who installs from stable is not upgraded to either release. Gate starting/exposing the service on a patched build or publish/upgrade the stable and rc package; handle existing installs too. Open #12271 proposes a security floor, so coordinate rather than silently treating 2026.516 as safe.
leads.triage: coordinator verified GHSA ranges in sol receipts; Opus independently confirmed against LizardByte repository advisories in self-check; published as 'Related, outside this change' note with LAN/Tailscale and local-only qualifiers; factual

leads.summary: Enabling the user unit retains a second, unmanaged Hyprland Sunshine start
leads.consequence: Enabling this unit installs it under graphical-session.target, while the now-successful installer appends o.launch_on_start("sunshine"). On a subsequent Hyprland start the session runs both the systemd user unit and uwsm-app -- sunshine. The extra process is not the unit and can race it for Sunshine's ports; the unit's Restart=on-failure may repeat the race. A re-run does not remove the line; after upgrades any existing exact line remains. Choose the systemd unit as the sole start path and remove legacy exact autostart entries, including existing installations. Open #12358, #12472, and #12271 attempt variations of this.
leads.triage: already in Opus final F1; corroborated; published; behavioural

leads.summary: Successful installation automatically launches a browser with a process-wide certificate-error bypass
leads.consequence: With Chromium selected (or as Omarchy's fallback), omarchy-webapp-install writes the custom command to Sunshine Admin.desktop and the installer executes it immediately. bin/omarchy-launch-webapp forwards --ignore-certificate-errors to the browser rather than restricting it to localhost. Chromium reads this flag from the browser process's command line in its WebAuthn security decision, so if Sunshine Admin launches the browser first, other browser windows in that process inherit the security bypass; the generated desktop shortcut repeats it on later launches. Remove the global flag and handle the localhost certificate explicitly. Related #12834 addresses this and migrates existing shortcuts; if it lands first this issue is addressed without conflicting with the new unit name.
leads.triage: pre-existing, unchanged by this PR, addressed by #12834; dropped as out of scope (not confirmed); behavioural

leads.summary: Tailscale installed after Sunshine never receives the promised streaming firewall rules
leads.consequence: With no tailscale0 when Sunshine is first installed, every Tailscale rule is silently skipped. Later omarchy-install-service-tailscale creates the service/interface but never reruns Sunshine's UFW setup. Stock firewall denies inbound by default, so Moonlight over Tailscale cannot connect until manually opening ports or rerunning the Sunshine installer. Opening ports only for currently present tailscale0 is a lifecycle gap, not proof that the new systemd call failed. Add the rules independent of interface existence or reconcile them when Tailscale becomes active.
leads.triage: coordinator confirmed install-service-tailscale does not touch ufw; pre-existing sequencing unrelated to the changed line; dropped as out of scope; factual

leads.summary: Sunshine installer and remover remain unregistered in the Install/Remove Service menu
leads.consequence: CLI and manual document omarchy install service sunshine, and the now-working command installs the package. But the menu's explicit Install > Service and Remove > Service groups have no Sunshine entries. A user browsing the GUI cannot discover install or invoke the matching cleanup from its service menu. This absence predates the one-line change but becomes visible as the install path is repaired. Add install.service.sunshine adjacent to line 227 and remove.service.sunshine adjacent to line 311, with package-presence guards and installer/remover actions consistent with the siblings.
leads.triage: pre-existing product choice unrelated to the change; dropped; factual

leads.summary: No kept test would detect regressing the unit argument back to the broken alias
leads.consequence: The one-line mutant systemctl --user enable --now sunshine passes the existing metadata/style and installed-service checks, which exercise CLI headers or Dropbox/Tailscale only. A sandbox fixture using the real installer with stubbed canonical-only systemctl yields base-tip fresh/rerun exit 1, skips webapp and autostart; head fresh/rerun exit 0 and reaches downstream setup. Keep a fixture asserting the real unit name and downstream actions on a fresh install and rerun, plus the matching removal path; another open PR (#8879) proposes such a test.
leads.triage: already in Opus final Q4 with base-fail/head-pass run; published as Optional test improvement; factual

leads.summary: Several open, divergent Sunshine fixes collide at this exact installer hunk; consolidate the intended behaviour
leads.consequence: #12505 repeats the one-line canonical-name fix; #13331 and #8879 additionally change the remover; #12358, #12472 and #12271 also eliminate the double start; #9011 adds Nvidia capture configuration but retains the short alias. All seven overlapping heads checked are divergent from this PR, not stacked; merges against the common original file produce conflict markers at the enable hunk. GitHub currently calls those branches mergeable against their respective base, which does not prove they can be merged together. If resolving #9011 by preserving its old enable command, the fresh-install failure returns despite this PR. Fold in the necessary remover/test/security/autostart work or avoid merging duplicate patches independently.
leads.triage: already in Opus final F3 (merge-tree runs); corroborated; published; factual

limits: The unit-file fixture uses systemctl --global --root with the shipped user unit, not a live user manager. It confirms fresh/canonical/repeated enable and alias disable symlink semantics, but does not demonstrate runtime Sunshine startup, port binding or --now stop behaviour.

Full test/cli returns 1 at both head and base tip in the command sandbox on the unrelated vscode generated theme symlink assertion (plan-tests/runs/20260927T100941Z-c9657d92); targeted CLI metadata, bin-style, installed-service and privileged-heredoc checks return 0 on both.

The Arch/AUR package recipe at upstream v2026.516.143833 is a template; the exact Omarchy binary archive, its metadata and installed unit were independently downloaded and read. No real host package state was queried.

flags.claim: After it, every new install starts Sunshine twice at login.
flags.why: Configuration observed (T1 tree: wants link + autostart line), launches not observed; rests on unit WantedBy, helpers.lua:113-125 and #12349/#7218 reports

flags.claim: Before this PR the installer never enabled the unit, so this did not matter.
flags.why: Only true for current packages. With the 2025.924 package (omarchy-pkgs 465c107, installer b486a439, both 2026-05-15) the old line enabled sunshine.service as the real unit (S8/T6). Users who applied the #12053 workaround have the unit enabled by the real name (T4), so the alias stop already failed for them.

flags.claim: Sunshine keeps running after the package is removed.
flags.why: Lost qualifier: my report says until logout (the user manager stops units at session end unless lingering).
Dropped output: the expected result from my report (non-zero status with 'Unit sunshine.service not loaded.', then 'active') is missing, so a reader cannot tell what confirms the claim.

flags.claim: stable installs will now start this build and open its streaming ports
flags.why: Ports are opened only to 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 and tailscale0 (script lines 8-10,19-36; T1 calls.log). GHSA-fp6g is local-only ('Network access alone is not sufficient'), and the package with its setcap .INSTALL is installed at line 73 at base too, so that issue is not newly exposed by the fix.
#12505 is +3/-1: the same command plus a two-line comment. Its merge-tree conflict with #13230 is in that comment. My report has the same wording.

flags.claim: #12358, #12472 and #12271 already do this (drop the call and its HYPR_* constants)
flags.why: Partly wrong: #12472 keeps the HYPR_* constants and reuses them in a new disable_hyprland_autostart that strips stray lines during install. #12358 and #12271 drop function, call and constants. The suggestion also omits the function definition.
Nitpick: ambiguous absolute. The packages have 130/131 members; the intended meaning is that this is the only systemd user unit.

flags.claim: A stubbed run of the installer fails at base and passes at head
flags.why: Nitpick: systemctl was the real client-side binary in my run (T3). With a fully stubbed systemctl (as in #8879) base exits 0 and only the log assertion fails. The conclusion about #8879's fixture holds.

flags.claim: Repository tests (bin-style-test.sh, bash -n) pass at base and head.
flags.why: Nitpick: bash -n is a syntax check I ran, not a repository test.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the new unit name is correct for the Sunshine packages Omarchy ships today, and it fixes both failures in #12053. Once the enable step succeeds, though, the rest of the installer adds a second way to start Sunshine at every login. The matching remover still uses the old alias. Several open PRs already change this same line.

**Verified:** package and systemd behaviour.
- `omarchy-pkg-add sunshine` installs from the `[omarchy]` repository (stable and rc: `2026.516.143833-4.1`; edge: `2026.914.233613-1`).
- Both packages ship a single user unit, `usr/lib/systemd/user/app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service`, with `Alias=sunshine.service` and `WantedBy=graphical-session.target`.
- Upstream Sunshine's own docs use the real unit name.

Results with the real `systemctl` (systemd 261.2) run client-side against the packaged unit, in a sandbox with a synthetic home:

| Case | Old line (`sunshine`) | New line (real name) |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh install | exit 1, `Unit sunshine.service does not exist` | exit 0, alias and `graphical-session.target.wants` links created |
| Re-run after the unit is enabled | exit 1, `Refusing to operate on linked unit file sunshine.service` | exit 0, no changes |
| Whole installer, external commands stubbed | stops at line 74; firewall, web app and autostart steps never run | completes all steps, and a re-run exits 0 |

### The fixed installer now sets up two start paths for Sunshine

With line 74 succeeding, the script now reaches `enable_hyprland_autostart` (lines 17, 63-70, 83-84). That step appends `o.launch_on_start("sunshine")` to `~/.config/hypr/autostart.lua`. `default/hypr/helpers.lua:113-125` runs it as `uwsm-app -- sunshine` when Hyprland starts. The enabled unit also starts Sunshine with the graphical session. After the sandboxed head install, both the unit link and the autostart line were present.

```text
login
 ├─ graphical-session.target ─> app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service ─> /usr/bin/sunshine
 └─ autostart.lua: o.launch_on_start("sunshine") ─> uwsm-app -- sunshine ─> /usr/bin/sunshine
```

**Impact:** before this PR, the enable step failed on a fresh install and the script exited before adding either start path. After it, every new install is set up to start Sunshine twice at each login. Open issues #12349 and #7218 report that one of the two copies aborts on each login. That crash was not reproduced here. `plans/remote.md` (lines 9 and 36) also treats the two start paths as a bug and names the unit as the one to keep.

**Suggested change:** drop the `enable_hyprland_autostart` function, its call and the `HYPR_*` constants from the installer in the same change. The remover's existing `sed` cleanup still removes lines already written. #12358 and #12271 already drop the autostart step, and #12358 adds a migration for existing installs. #12472 instead strips stray autostart lines during install.

### The remover still disables by the alias

`bin/omarchy-remove-service-sunshine:62` still runs `systemctl --user disable --now sunshine 2>/dev/null || true`. In the sandbox, `disable` through the alias removes the same links as the real name, so the disable half works.

**Impact (from systemd 261.2 source, not run against a live user manager):** `systemctl` reloads the user manager after disabling and only then sends the `--now` stop to `sunshine.service`. That reload drops the alias, because the alias symlink was just deleted. The stop then likely fails with `Unit sunshine.service not loaded.`, the script discards the error, and Sunshine keeps running until logout after the package is removed. With current packages, the installer at base never enabled the unit, so this only affected users who had enabled it by hand (for example with the #12053 workaround). After this PR it affects every install.

To confirm on a real session after a head install:

```bash
systemctl --user disable --now sunshine; echo $?
systemctl --user is-active app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service
```

The expected result, if the source reading is right, is a non-zero exit with `Unit sunshine.service not loaded.`, followed by `active`.

**Suggested change:** use `app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service` on line 62 as well, as #8879, #13331, #12472 and #12358 do.

### Overlapping open PRs

- #12505 makes the same command change, plus a two-line comment.
- #8879 changes both the install and remove lines and adds `test/shell.d/sunshine-service-test.sh`. When closing #11352, #9979, #9104 and #7359 on 2026-09-20, a maintainer kept #8879 open to consolidate this fix.
- #13331, #12505, #12472, #8879, #12358, #12271 and #9011 each merge cleanly into `quattro` on their own, but each conflicts with this PR at the same installer hunk.
- The new line also resolves the open duplicate issues #12499, #12537 and #7050. It does not resolve #12349 or #7218 (the double start above).

**Related, outside this change:** stable and rc still ship Sunshine `2026.516.143833`, and published upstream advisories list that version as affected: five fixed in `2026.906.222525`, and a Linux capability issue fixed in `2026.914.233613`. With the installer fixed, stable installs will now start this build and open its streaming ports to private LANs and Tailscale. (The capability issue is local-only, and the package is already installed at base.) #12271 proposes a version floor.

**Optional test improvement:** no test covers either Sunshine script. A run of the installer with its external commands stubbed (the real `systemctl` client-side) fails at base and passes at head, so a small fixture like the one in #8879 would catch a return to the alias.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head commit against the current `quattro` tip, the Omarchy `sunshine` packages (stable and edge, checked against the repository database hashes), upstream Sunshine packaging, and systemd 261.2 source. `systemctl` enable and disable ran client-side in a sandbox with a synthetic home. The install script ran with the package, firewall, web app and `sudo` commands stubbed. No live user manager, Sunshine daemon or desktop session was run, so `--now` start and stop, the double-start crash and the remover's stop failure were not observed. `bin-style-test.sh` and a `bash -n` syntax check pass at base and head. `test/cli` stops at the same unrelated environment check at both, before its metadata lint.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
